subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Parker Solar Probe
description: Learn The Parker Solar Probe in one minute.

hook.text: The Parker Solar Probe flies closer to the Sun than any spacecraft ever—plunging into the corona itself.

buildup.text: At closest approach, it endures 1,370°C behind a heat shield just 11.4 cm thick.

discovery.text: It found magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind—sudden field reversals that accelerate particles outward.

twist.text: The probe hits 690,000 km/h—fast enough to fly from New York to Tokyo in under a minute.

climax.text: Understanding the corona helps predict space weather that can knock out power grids on Earth.

punchline.text: Touching the Sun. The fastest thing humans ever built.

quiz.question: What is the Parker Solar Probe designed to study?
options: The Sun's corona and the origin of the solar wind
The surface composition of the Sun's photosphere
Solar eclipses from orbit around the Sun

details.summary: Launched in 2018, NASA's Parker Solar Probe is the fastest human-made object and the closest spacecraft to the Sun, diving within 6.1 million kilometers of the solar surface.
details.whyItMatters: Parker Solar Probe is answering longstanding mysteries: why the corona is hundreds of times hotter than the surface and how the solar wind is accelerated. Its data improves space weather forecasting to protect Earth's technology infrastructure.
takeaways: Parker Solar Probe flies within 6.1 million km of the Sun
It's the fastest human-made object at 700,000+ km/h
It's solving mysteries of the corona's extreme heat

faq.question: How does the probe survive so close to the Sun?
faq.answer: A 11.4-centimeter-thick carbon composite heat shield keeps the spacecraft in shadow while the Sun-facing side reaches about 1,370°C. The instruments behind the shield operate near room temperature. The shield is made of lightweight carbon foam sandwiched between carbon-carbon composite plates.

faq.question: What has Parker Solar Probe discovered?
faq.answer: Switchbacks — sudden reversals in the solar wind's magnetic field — were an unexpected discovery. It also found that the solar wind near the Sun is far more structured and turbulent than expected. The probe has flown through the Sun's corona itself, directly sampling solar material.
